candidates.comment: A rating value relation between a rating and its numerical or textual score. Also called score, rating score, value of rating. Examples: "A movie review has a rating value of 4.5.", "A product has a rating value of 'Excellent'.", "A restaurant has a rating value of 3 stars."

candidates.label: aggregateRating
candidates.comment: An aggregate rating relation between an item (e.g., product, service, creative work) and its overall rating derived from multiple reviews. Also called overall score, collective rating, average review. Examples: "A product's aggregate rating is '4.5 stars'.", "A movie's aggregate rating is '8.2/10'."

candidates.label: bestRating
candidates.comment: A number or text representing the highest value allowed in a rating system. Also called: maximum rating, top score, highest possible rating. Examples: "Rating 'Product Review' bestRating '5'", "Rating 'Movie Score' bestRating '10'". Distinct from worstRating, which is the lowest value.

candidates.label: reviewRating
candidates.comment: The specific rating provided within a review. Also called rating in review, review's score, individual rating. Examples: `Customer Review` reviewRating `5 stars`, `Film Critic Review` reviewRating `8/10`, `Restaurant Review` reviewRating `3 out of 5`. Distinct from `aggregateRating`, which is the overall rating of the review *as a creative work*, not the rating *given by* the review.

candidates.label: ratingCount
candidates.comment: A rating count relation between an aggregate rating and the total number of individual ratings contributing to it. Also called number of ratings, total ratings. Examples: "An aggregate rating has a rating count of 150.", "A product review summary has a rating count of 500.", "A movie's average rating has a rating count of 10,000."

candidates.label: upvoteCount
candidates.comment: An upvote count relation between a comment and the number of upvotes it has received. Also called positive votes, likes count, approval count. Examples: "Comment upvoteCount '15'", "Answer upvoteCount '100'", "Question upvoteCount '5'".

candidates.label: reviewCount
candidates.comment: The total number of individual reviews contributing to an aggregate rating. Also called total reviews, number of reviews, review tally. Examples: `Product Aggregate Rating` reviewCount `150`, `Movie Aggregate Rating` reviewCount `5000`, `Service Aggregate Rating` reviewCount `75`.

candidates.label: musicBy
candidates.comment: A composer or music group responsible for the soundtrack of a creative work. Also called soundtrack by, composer of, musical score by. Examples: "Movie X musicBy 'John Williams'", "TV Series Y musicBy 'Ramin Djawadi'", "Video Game Z musicBy 'Koji Kondo'". Distinct from composer, which is for the composer of a MusicComposition.

candidates.label: downvoteCount
candidates.comment: A downvote count relation between a comment and the integer representing the number of downvotes it has received. Also called "dislike count", "negative votes". Examples: "Comment 'This is wrong' downvoteCount '5'", "Answer downvoteCount '2'", "Review downvoteCount '10'".

candidates.label: award
candidates.comment: An award won by or for a creative work, organization, person, product, or service. Also called: honor, prize, recognition. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Movie' award 'Oscar'", "Organization 'Company X' award 'Best Employer'", "Person 'Scientist' award 'Nobel Prize'". Distinct from awards, which is the plural form.

relations.embedding_query_text: helpedTeam:

chosen_property.label: helpedTeam
chosen_property.definition: Indicates the sports team that a person helped.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property directly indicates a Person helping a SportsTeam.

candidates.label: awayTeam
candidates.comment: A person or sports team designated as the away team in a sports event. Also called: visiting team, opponent. Examples: "SportsEvent 'Football Match' awayTeam 'Team B'", "SportsEvent 'Basketball Game' awayTeam 'Lakers'". Distinct from homeTeam, which is the team playing at their home venue.

candidates.label: sportsTeam
candidates.comment: A participation relation between an exercise action and the sports team involved in it. Also called "team participated", "team involved", "athletic team". Examples: "The goal was scored by the sportsTeam Real Madrid", "The race involved sportsTeam Team USA", "This action was performed by a sportsTeam.". Distinct from participant, which is a more general participant property.

candidates.label: homeTeam
candidates.comment: A home team relation between a sports event and the team or person designated as the home participant. Also called host team, home side, local team. Examples: "A sports event has a home team 'Lions'.", "The match features a home team.", "This event's home team is a specific person."

candidates.label: athlete
candidates.comment: A person who is a performing member of a sports team. Also called: player, team member, sportsman/sportswoman. Examples: "SportsTeam 'Lakers' athlete 'LeBron James'", "SportsTeam 'Red Sox' athlete 'Mookie Betts'", "SportsTeam 'National Team' athlete 'Megan Rapinoe'". Distinct from coach, which is a non-playing role.

candidates.label: softwareHelp
candidates.comment: A relation between a software application and a creative work providing assistance or guidance for its use. Also called "application help", "software documentation", "user guide for software". Examples: "Microsoft Word has softwareHelp a user manual", "The app's softwareHelp is an online FAQ", "This softwareHelp explains how to use the program."

candidates.label: productSupported
candidates.comment: A support relation between a contact point and the product or service it provides support for. Also called supports product, provides support for, related to product. Examples: "Apple Support contact point supports iPhone.", "Microsoft customer service supports Windows.", "Help desk supports enterprise software."

candidates.label: fundedItem
candidates.comment: A funded item relation between a grant and the biochemical entity, creative work, event, medical entity, organization, person, or product that receives direct or indirect funding or sponsorship. Also called: grant recipient, sponsored item, supported entity. Examples: "Research Grant" funded item "Cancer Research Project", "Arts Grant" funded item "Local Theater Production", "Educational Grant" funded item "Student Scholarship Program". Distinct from funding, which is the grant itself.

candidates.label: providesService
candidates.comment: A service provision relation between a service channel and the specific service it delivers. Also called channel delivers, service offered via, offers service. Examples: "An online portal provides service 'customer support'.", "A phone line provides service 'technical assistance'.", "A mobile app provides service 'online banking'."

candidates.label: sponsor
candidates.comment: A support relation between an entity (creative work, event, grant, study, organization, or person) and the person or organization providing financial or other backing. Also called "funded by", "supported by", "patron", "underwritten by". Examples: "The event has sponsor Acme Corp", "The medical study's sponsor is the NIH", "This artist has sponsor a private foundation."

candidates.label: participant
candidates.comment: A collaborative relation between an action and an organization or person who indirectly participated in it. Also called collaborated with, involved, assisted by, co-agent. Examples: A writing action has a participant co-author. A research project has a participant researcher. A meeting has a participant attendee. Distinct from agent, which is the primary actor of an action.

relations.definition: Indicates an entity that received an advantage or positive outcome.
relations.embedding_query_text: benefits: Indicates an entity that received an advantage or positive outcome.

chosen_property.label: benefitsTeam
chosen_property.definition: Indicates the sports team that received an advantage or positive outcome from a sports referee decision.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property directly indicates a SportsRefereeDecision benefiting a SportsTeam.

candidates.label: positiveNotes
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute providing positive considerations, highlights, or pros for a product or an item being reviewed. Also called pros, advantages, benefits, highlights. Examples: A product has positive notes like 'Excellent battery life'. A review has positive notes like 'User-friendly interface'. The service has positive notes like 'Responsive customer support'. Distinct from negativeNotes, which provides negative considerations.

candidates.label: physiologicalBenefits
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute detailing the specific physiological benefits associated with a diet plan. Also called health advantages, bodily benefits, wellness effects. Examples: A diet has physiological benefits like 'improved cardiovascular health'. A diet has physiological benefits like 'weight loss'. A diet has physiological benefits like 'reduced inflammation'.

candidates.label: hasTierBenefit
candidates.comment: A tier benefit relation between a member program tier and a specific benefit associated with that tier. Also called tier advantage, member perk, program benefit. Examples: "A loyalty program tier has a tier benefit of free shipping.", "The premium tier has a tier benefit of exclusive access.", "This tier offers a tier benefit of bonus points."

candidates.label: jobBenefits
candidates.comment: An employment perk relation between a job posting and the description of advantages or entitlements offered with the position. Also called employee benefits, job perks, compensation package, employment advantages. Examples: A job posting lists jobBenefits as 'Health insurance, 401k, paid time off'. A job posting includes jobBenefits like 'flexible hours and remote work option'. A job posting details jobBenefits such as 'gym membership and free meals'. Distinct from salaryCurrency or baseSalary, which are about monetary compensation.

candidates.label: negativeNotes
candidates.comment: Negative considerations or drawbacks associated with a product or described in a review. Also called cons, disadvantages, downsides, criticisms. Examples: "Product X negativeNotes 'short battery life'", "Review Y negativeNotes 'poor customer service'", "Software Z negativeNotes 'steep learning curve', 'frequent crashes'". Distinct from positiveNotes, which describes favorable aspects.

candidates.label: benefits
candidates.comment: A description of benefits associated with a job posting. Also called: job perks, employee benefits, compensation package details. Examples: "JobPosting 'Marketing Manager' benefits 'Health insurance, 401k, paid time off'", "JobPosting 'Developer' benefits 'Flexible hours, remote work option'."

candidates.label: cashBack
candidates.comment: A benefit offered by a payment card, indicating whether cashback is available and its percentage or value. Also called "cash rebate", "cash rewards", "cash return". Examples: "Credit card cashBack 2%", "Debit card cashBack true", "Payment card cashBack 0.01".

candidates.label: incentiveAmount
candidates.comment: An incentive amount relation between a financial incentive and the value that can be redeemed. Also called incentive value, redeemable amount, benefit amount. Examples: "A financial incentive has an incentive amount of $500.", "The incentive offers an incentive amount as a percentage.", "This incentive provides an incentive amount as a loan."

candidates.label: adverseOutcome
candidates.comment: An adverse outcome relation between a medical device or therapeutic procedure and a possible complication or side effect. Also called side effect, complication, negative reaction. Examples: "A surgery's adverse outcome is 'infection'.", "A medical device's adverse outcome is 'skin irritation'." Distinct from seriousAdverseOutcome, which is specifically for life-threatening or severe complications.

candidates.label: incentiveType
candidates.comment: An incentive type relation between a financial incentive and the specific type of incentive offered. Also called type of benefit, incentive category, subsidy type. Examples: "A financial incentive has an incentive type 'tax credit'.", "The program offers an incentive type 'rebate'.", "This incentive is a 'subsidy' incentive type."

relations.embedding_query_text: helpedBy:

chosen_property.label: helpedByDecision
chosen_property.definition: Indicates the sports referee decision that provided assistance or a positive influence to a sports team.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property directly indicates a SportsTeam being helped by a SportsRefereeDecision.

candidates.label: offeredBy
candidates.comment: An organization or person making an offer. Also called provided by, seller, vendor, offered from. Examples: "Product Offer offeredBy 'Acme Corp'", "Service Offer offeredBy 'John Doe'", "Event Ticket Offer offeredBy 'Ticketmaster'". Distinct from seller, which is a more specific term for a person or organization selling something.

candidates.label: issuedBy
candidates.comment: An issuing authority relation between a certification, permit, or ticket and the organization that granted or provided it. Also called granted by, provided by, authorized by, issuer. Examples: A driver's license is issuedBy 'Department of Motor Vehicles'. A concert ticket is issuedBy 'Ticketmaster'. A professional certification is issuedBy 'Certification Body X'.

candidates.label: reviewedBy
candidates.comment: The person or organization responsible for reviewing the content of a webpage for accuracy or completeness. Also called content reviewer, page editor, accuracy checker. Examples: `Medical Information Page` reviewedBy `Dr. Jane Doe`, `News Article` reviewedBy `Fact-Checking Organization`, `Research Paper` reviewedBy `Peer Review Board`. Distinct from `author`, which indicates who created the content, not who reviewed it.

candidates.label: musicBy
candidates.comment: A composer or music group responsible for the soundtrack of a creative work. Also called soundtrack by, composer of, musical score by. Examples: "Movie X musicBy 'John Williams'", "TV Series Y musicBy 'Ramin Djawadi'", "Video Game Z musicBy 'Koji Kondo'". Distinct from composer, which is for the composer of a MusicComposition.

candidates.label: readBy
candidates.comment: A narration relation between an audiobook and the person who performs the reading. Also called narrated by, performed by, voiced by. Examples: "The audiobook 'Harry Potter' is read by 'Stephen Fry'.", "An autobiography audiobook is read by 'the author'.", "A classic novel audiobook is read by 'a professional narrator'."

candidates.label: publishedBy
candidates.comment: A publisher relation between a publication event and the organization or person responsible for it. Also called published by, issued by, released by. Examples: "A book's publication event was published by 'Penguin Random House'.", "A journal article's publication event was published by 'Elsevier'.", "A blog post's publication event was published by 'Jane Doe'.". Distinct from publisher, which refers to the publisher of the creative work itself.

candidates.label: legislationPassedBy
candidates.comment: A passing authority relation between a piece of legislation and the organization or person that originally enacted it. Also called: enacted by, made by, legislated by. Examples: "Primary Legislation legislationPassedBy Parliament", "Secondary Legislation legislationPassedBy Government", "Local Bylaw legislationPassedBy City Council". Distinct from legislationResponsible, which refers to the ministry or individual in charge of elaborating or addressing questions about the legislation.

candidates.label: affectedBy
candidates.comment: An affected by relation between a medical test and the drugs that can influence its results. Also called influenced by, impacted by, drug interaction. Examples: "A blood test's results are affected by 'anticoagulants'.", "The diagnostic test is affected by 'caffeine'."

candidates.label: recognizedBy
candidates.comment: A recognition relation between a credential and the organization that acknowledges its validity or value. Also called accredited by, validated by, acknowledged by. Examples: "A university degree is recognized by 'the Ministry of Education'.", "A professional certification is recognized by 'an industry association'.", "A medical license is recognized by 'the Medical Board'."

candidates.label: geoCoveredBy
candidates.comment: A geo covered by relation representing a spatial relationship where a geometry or place is entirely covered by another geometry or place. Also called: is covered by, lies within, is contained by. Examples: "City 'Paris'" geo covered by "Country 'France'", "Lake 'Superior'" geo covered by "North America", "House '123 Main St'" geo covered by "City 'Springfield'". Distinct from geoCovers, which is the inverse relation.

relations.embedding_query_text: playsFor:

chosen_property.label: worksFor
chosen_property.justification: The 'worksFor' property indicates the organization a person is employed by, and SportsTeam is a type of Organization.

candidates.label: playMode
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the supported gameplay modes for a video game or series, such as single-player, multi-player, or co-op. Also called game mode, player configuration, gameplay style. Examples: A video game has a play mode of 'SinglePlayer'. A video game has a play mode of 'MultiPlayer'. A video game has a play mode of 'CoOp'.

candidates.label: validFor
candidates.comment: A valid for relation between a credential or permit and the duration of its validity. Also called duration of validity, valid period, effective duration. Examples: "Permit validFor 'P1Y'", "Credential validFor 'P5Y'", "License validFor 'P6M'".

candidates.label: isConsumableFor
candidates.comment: A product dependency relation between a product and the other products that consume it or require it for operation. Also called consumable for, used by, required by, compatible consumable. Examples: An ink cartridge isConsumableFor 'Printer Model X'. Coffee pods areConsumableFor 'Coffee Machine Y'. Batteries areConsumableFor 'Remote Control Z'. Distinct from isAccessoryOrSparePartFor, which refers to items that are not used up.

candidates.label: worksFor
candidates.comment: An employment relation between a person and an organization, indicating the organization for which the person is employed. Also called employed by, affiliated with, works at, employed at. Examples: Employee worksFor CompanyA, Consultant worksFor AgencyB, Professor worksFor UniversityC. Distinct from memberOf, which indicates general membership in a group, not necessarily employment.

candidates.label: isAccessoryOrSparePartFor
candidates.comment: A product compatibility relation between a product and the other products for which it serves as an accessory or spare part. Also called accessory for, spare part for, compatible with, used with. Examples: A phone case isAccessoryOrSparePartFor 'iPhone 15'. A replacement battery isAccessoryOrSparePartFor 'Laptop Model X'. A camera lens isAccessoryOrSparePartFor 'DSLR Camera Y'. Distinct from isConsumableFor, which refers to items that are used up.

candidates.label: reservationFor
candidates.comment: A reservation for relation between a reservation and the specific item or service being booked. Also called booked item, reserved item, subject of reservation. Examples: "A reservation is for 'Flight BA249'.", "A restaurant booking is for 'Dinner at The Fancy Bistro'.", "A hotel reservation is for 'Room 301'."

candidates.label: gameServer
candidates.comment: A game server relation between a video game and the server where it can be played. Also called: hosted on, playable server, game host. Examples: "Minecraft" game server "Hypixel Network", "World of Warcraft" game server "Frostmourne Realm", "Call of Duty" game server "Dedicated Server". Distinct from game, which is the game itself.

candidates.label: inPlaylist
candidates.comment: A playlist inclusion relation between a music recording and the music playlist it belongs to. Also called part of playlist, on playlist, playlist track. Examples: "A music recording is in a playlist titled 'Workout Mix'.", "The song is in a playlist.", "This recording belongs to a specific playlist.". Distinct from inAlbum, which refers to a music album.

candidates.label: numberOfPlayers
candidates.comment: The number of people who can play a game or video game series, often expressed as a minimum, maximum, or range. Also called player count, game capacity, participant number. Examples: "Board Game X numberOfPlayers '2-4'", "Video Game Y numberOfPlayers '1 (single-player)'", "Online Game Z numberOfPlayers '100 (max)'".

candidates.label: actor
candidates.comment: An actor relation between a creative work (e.g., movie, episode, video game) or event and a person or performing group who performs in it. Also called performer, cast member, player. Examples: "A movie's actor is 'Tom Hanks'.", "A play's actor is 'The Ensemble Theatre'.", "An episode's actor is 'Jane Doe'." Distinct from actors, which is a deprecated property for the same concept.

relations.embedding_query_text: isA:

chosen_property.label: hasDesignation
chosen_property.definition: Indicates a designation or role that a sports team holds.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property directly indicates a SportsTeam having a Designation or Role.

candidates.label: isAvailableGenerically
candidates.comment: A drug availability relation indicating whether a drug is available in a generic formulation. Also called generic form available, generic equivalent, generic option. Examples: A drug has isAvailableGenerically set to 'true'. A brand-name medication has isAvailableGenerically set to 'false'. A common painkiller has isAvailableGenerically set to 'true'. Distinct from isProprietary, which indicates if the *name* is proprietary.

candidates.label: isAcceptingNewPatients
candidates.comment: A patient status relation indicating whether a medical organization is currently accepting new patients. Also called accepting new patients, open to new patients, taking new patients. Examples: A clinic has isAcceptingNewPatients set to 'true'. A hospital has isAcceptingNewPatients set to 'false'. A doctor's office has isAcceptingNewPatients set to 'true'.

candidates.label: isAccessibleForFree
candidates.comment: An access cost relation indicating whether a creative work, event, or place can be accessed without charge. Also called free access, no charge, complimentary access, free of cost. Examples: A public park has isAccessibleForFree set to 'true'. An online article has isAccessibleForFree set to 'true'. A concert has isAccessibleForFree set to 'false'.

candidates.label: isAccessoryOrSparePartFor
candidates.comment: A product compatibility relation between a product and the other products for which it serves as an accessory or spare part. Also called accessory for, spare part for, compatible with, used with. Examples: A phone case isAccessoryOrSparePartFor 'iPhone 15'. A replacement battery isAccessoryOrSparePartFor 'Laptop Model X'. A camera lens isAccessoryOrSparePartFor 'DSLR Camera Y'. Distinct from isConsumableFor, which refers to items that are used up.

candidates.label: isProprietary
candidates.comment: A naming status relation indicating whether a dietary supplement or drug is identified by a proprietary or brand name. Also called brand name, proprietary name, trademarked name. Examples: A drug has isProprietary set to 'true' (e.g., Tylenol). A dietary supplement has isProprietary set to 'false' (e.g., Acetaminophen). A medication has isProprietary set to 'true'. Distinct from isAvailableGenerically, which indicates if a generic *form* exists, not if the *name* itself is proprietary.

candidates.label: iso6523Code
candidates.comment: An organization identification relation between an organization and its globally standardized ISO 6523 code. Also called ISO 6523 identifier, organization code, international organization ID. Examples: An organization has an iso6523Code of '0060:802000000'. A company has an iso6523Code of '0199:LEI1234567890'. A business has an iso6523Code of '0088:1234567890123'. Distinct from leiCode, duns, globalLocationNumber, vatID, or taxID, as this is a more general, structured international identifier that can encompass those.

candidates.label: gtin8
candidates.comment: A GTIN-8 relation identifying a demand, offer, or product with its 8-digit Global Trade Item Number, also known as EAN-8. Also called: EAN-8, GTIN-8 identifier, 8-digit barcode. Examples: "Small Retail Item" gtin8 "12345670", "Confectionery Product" gtin8 "98765432", "Offer for Small Product" gtin8 "00000001". Distinct from gtin, which is the general GTIN.

candidates.label: inChI
candidates.comment: An InChI identifier relation between a molecular entity and its non-proprietary International Chemical Identifier. Also called chemical identifier, molecular ID, InChI string. Examples: "A molecular entity has an InChI identifier.", "The compound is identified by its InChI.", "This entity's InChI is a unique string."

candidates.label: isrcCode
candidates.comment: A music recording identification relation between a music recording and its International Standard Recording Code. Also called ISRC identifier, recording code, music track ID. Examples: A music recording has an isrcCode of 'US-S1Z-99-00001'. A song has an isrcCode of 'GB-LFB-04-00001'. An album track has an isrcCode of 'QZ-F89-12-00001'. Distinct from iswcCode, which is for musical compositions, not recordings.

candidates.label: gtin13
candidates.comment: A GTIN-13 relation identifying a demand, offer, or product with its 13-digit Global Trade Item Number, equivalent to EAN-13 or ISBN. Also called: EAN-13, ISBN-13, GTIN-13 identifier. Examples: "Book Product" gtin13 "9781234567890", "European Retail Item" gtin13 "5012345678901", "Offer for Book" gtin13 "9780123456789". Distinct from gtin, which is the general GTIN.

relations.embedding_query_text: reliedOn:

chosen_property.label: reliedOnPerson
chosen_property.definition: Indicates a person that a sports team relied upon for support or assistance.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property directly indicates a SportsTeam relying on a Person.

candidates.label: publishedOn
candidates.comment: A broadcast publication relation between a publication event and the broadcast service on which it was published. Also called aired on, broadcast via, released on service. Examples: "A TV show's publication event was published on 'BBC One'.", "A radio program's publication event was published on 'NPR'.", "A news segment's publication event was published on 'CNN'."

candidates.label: addOn
candidates.comment: An add-on relation between a base offer and an additional offer that can only be acquired in conjunction with it. Also called supplementary offer, bundled offer, extra option. Examples: "A car purchase offer has an add-on for extended warranty.", "A software license offer has an add-on for premium support."

candidates.label: isRelatedTo
candidates.comment: A general association relation between two products or services that have some unspecified connection. Also called associated with, connected to, linked to, relevant to. Examples: A smartphone isRelatedTo 'a smart watch'. A car service isRelatedTo 'car insurance'. A book isRelatedTo 'a movie adaptation'. Distinct from isSimilarTo, which implies functional similarity, and isAccessoryOrSparePartFor or isConsumableFor, which imply specific functional dependencies. This is a very general relation.

candidates.label: dependencies
candidates.comment: A prerequisite relation between a tech article and the requirements needed to fulfill its steps. Also called: technical requirements, prerequisites, required components. Examples: "Software Installation Guide" dependencies "Python 3.8, pip", "Hardware Setup Article" dependencies "Screwdriver, Internet connection", "Programming Tutorial" dependencies "Basic understanding of algorithms".

candidates.label: softwareRequirements
candidates.comment: A dependency relation between a software application and other software, text, or URLs specifying necessary components for its operation. Also called "application dependencies", "required software", "system requirements", "prerequisites". Examples: "Game X has softwareRequirements DirectX 12", "This application's softwareRequirements include Java Runtime Environment", "The softwareRequirements list specific operating system versions."

candidates.label: durationOfWarranty
candidates.comment: A warranty duration relation between a warranty promise and the quantitative value representing its length. Also called "warranty period", "guarantee length", "coverage duration". Examples: "Laptop warranty durationOfWarranty 'P1Y'", "Car warranty durationOfWarranty 'P3Y'", "Appliance warranty durationOfWarranty 'P6M'". Distinct from duration, which is a general property for the length of various items.

candidates.label: isConsumableFor
candidates.comment: A product dependency relation between a product and the other products that consume it or require it for operation. Also called consumable for, used by, required by, compatible consumable. Examples: An ink cartridge isConsumableFor 'Printer Model X'. Coffee pods areConsumableFor 'Coffee Machine Y'. Batteries areConsumableFor 'Remote Control Z'. Distinct from isAccessoryOrSparePartFor, which refers to items that are not used up.

candidates.label: constraintProperty
candidates.comment: A definitional relation for a constraint node, indicating a property used as a constraint. Also called "constraining property", "restricted by property", "property constraint". Examples: "Statistical variable constraint node constraintProperty 'schema:age'", "Data filter constraintProperty 'dc:gender'".

candidates.label: isBasedOn
candidates.comment: A derivation relation between a creative work and the resource (another work, product, or URL) from which it is adapted or modified. Also called derived from, adapted from, based on, inspired by, modification of. Examples: A movie isBasedOn 'a novel'. A software update isBasedOn 'previous version'. A remix isBasedOn 'original song'. Distinct from isBasedOnUrl, which specifically points to a URL as the source.

candidates.label: worksFor
candidates.comment: An employment relation between a person and an organization, indicating the organization for which the person is employed. Also called employed by, affiliated with, works at, employed at. Examples: Employee worksFor CompanyA, Consultant worksFor AgencyB, Professor worksFor UniversityC. Distinct from memberOf, which indicates general membership in a group, not necessarily employment.

relations.embedding_query_text: manages:

chosen_property.label: coach
chosen_property.justification: The 'coach' property runs from SportsTeam to Person. 'manages' is the inverse, from SportsCoach (Person) to SportsTeam.

candidates.label: programmingModel
candidates.comment: A programming model relation between an API reference and its management paradigm (managed or unmanaged). Also called API model, management type. Examples: "A .NET API has a programming model 'managed'.", "A C++ library API has a programming model 'unmanaged'.", "A Java API has a programming model 'managed'."

candidates.label: maintainer
candidates.comment: A maintainer relation between a creative work and the person or organization that manages its contributions and/or publication. Also called: project manager, curator, responsible party. Examples: "Software Package maintainer John Doe", "Dataset maintainer Open Data Initiative", "Website maintainer Webmaster Team".

candidates.label: hostingOrganization
candidates.comment: A hosting organization relation between a member program or program membership and the organization that offers or manages it. Also called program provider, membership organization, host company. Examples: "A member program has a hosting organization 'Airline X'.", "The program membership is with a hosting organization.", "This program is hosted by a specific organization."

candidates.label: coach
candidates.comment: A leadership relation between a sports team and the person who acts as its coach. Also called "team coach", "trainer", "manager". Examples: "Basketball team coach John Smith", "Soccer team coach Jane Doe".

candidates.label: serviceOperator
candidates.comment: The organization responsible for operating a government service, distinct from the primary provider. Also called service management, operating entity, service subcontractor. Examples: `Public Transport Service` serviceOperator `Transit Authority`, `Waste Collection Service` serviceOperator `Private Waste Management Company`, `National Park Service` serviceOperator `Local Park Management`. Distinct from `provider`, which is the primary organization offering the service.

candidates.label: landlord
candidates.comment: A property ownership relation between a rent action and the person or organization that owns and leases the real estate. Also called property owner, lessor, rental owner, proprietor. Examples: A rent action has a landlord of 'John Doe'. A rent action has a landlord of 'Property Management Inc.'. A lease agreement lists 'Sarah Smith' as the landlord. Distinct from agent, which is the general actor of an action.

candidates.label: accessibilityControl
candidates.comment: An accessibility control relation between a creative work and the input methods sufficient for its full control. Also called control methods, input compatibility, interaction modes. Examples: "A video game's accessibility control is 'keyboard'.", "A web application's accessibility control is 'mouse'."

candidates.label: nerveMotor
candidates.comment: A muscle controlled by a nerve through a neurological pathway. Also called motor innervation, controls muscle, innervates muscle. Examples: "Radial Nerve nerveMotor 'Triceps Brachii'", "Musculocutaneous Nerve nerveMotor 'Biceps Brachii'", "Phrenic Nerve nerveMotor 'Diaphragm'". Distinct from nerve, which describes the nerve of a muscle.

candidates.label: organizer
candidates.comment: An organization or person responsible for organizing an event. Also called event planner, host, coordinator, promoter. Examples: "Conference X organizer 'Acme Events Inc.'", "Concert Y organizer 'Live Nation'", "Workshop Z organizer 'Jane Doe'". Distinct from performer, who participates in the event.

candidates.label: makesOffer
candidates.comment: An offering relation between an organization or person and the offer for products or services they provide. Also called: offers, provides, sells. Examples: "Retailer makesOffer Discounted Electronics", "Consultant makesOffer Business Strategy Services", "Restaurant makesOffer Dinner Menu".

relations.embedding_query_text: fouledBy:

chosen_property.label: fouledBy
chosen_property.definition: Indicates the person who committed a foul against another person.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property directly indicates a Person being fouled by another Person.

candidates.label: legislationPassedBy
candidates.comment: A passing authority relation between a piece of legislation and the organization or person that originally enacted it. Also called: enacted by, made by, legislated by. Examples: "Primary Legislation legislationPassedBy Parliament", "Secondary Legislation legislationPassedBy Government", "Local Bylaw legislationPassedBy City Council". Distinct from legislationResponsible, which refers to the ministry or individual in charge of elaborating or addressing questions about the legislation.

candidates.label: legislationCountersignedBy
candidates.comment: A countersignature relation between a piece of legislation and the person or organization that countersigned it. Also called: countersigned by, officially endorsed by, co-signed by. Examples: "The Bill of Rights legislationCountersignedBy President Washington", "EU Directive 2023/45 legislationCountersignedBy European Commission", "Local Ordinance legislationCountersignedBy City Clerk".

candidates.label: issuedBy
candidates.comment: An issuing authority relation between a certification, permit, or ticket and the organization that granted or provided it. Also called granted by, provided by, authorized by, issuer. Examples: A driver's license is issuedBy 'Department of Motor Vehicles'. A concert ticket is issuedBy 'Ticketmaster'. A professional certification is issuedBy 'Certification Body X'.

candidates.label: affectedBy
candidates.comment: An affected by relation between a medical test and the drugs that can influence its results. Also called influenced by, impacted by, drug interaction. Examples: "A blood test's results are affected by 'anticoagulants'.", "The diagnostic test is affected by 'caffeine'."

candidates.label: musicBy
candidates.comment: A composer or music group responsible for the soundtrack of a creative work. Also called soundtrack by, composer of, musical score by. Examples: "Movie X musicBy 'John Williams'", "TV Series Y musicBy 'Ramin Djawadi'", "Video Game Z musicBy 'Koji Kondo'". Distinct from composer, which is for the composer of a MusicComposition.

candidates.label: readBy
candidates.comment: A narration relation between an audiobook and the person who performs the reading. Also called narrated by, performed by, voiced by. Examples: "The audiobook 'Harry Potter' is read by 'Stephen Fry'.", "An autobiography audiobook is read by 'the author'.", "A classic novel audiobook is read by 'a professional narrator'."

candidates.label: reviewedBy
candidates.comment: The person or organization responsible for reviewing the content of a webpage for accuracy or completeness. Also called content reviewer, page editor, accuracy checker. Examples: `Medical Information Page` reviewedBy `Dr. Jane Doe`, `News Article` reviewedBy `Fact-Checking Organization`, `Research Paper` reviewedBy `Peer Review Board`. Distinct from `author`, which indicates who created the content, not who reviewed it.

candidates.label: publishedBy
candidates.comment: A publisher relation between a publication event and the organization or person responsible for it. Also called published by, issued by, released by. Examples: "A book's publication event was published by 'Penguin Random House'.", "A journal article's publication event was published by 'Elsevier'.", "A blog post's publication event was published by 'Jane Doe'.". Distinct from publisher, which refers to the publisher of the creative work itself.

candidates.label: offeredBy
candidates.comment: An organization or person making an offer. Also called provided by, seller, vendor, offered from. Examples: "Product Offer offeredBy 'Acme Corp'", "Service Offer offeredBy 'John Doe'", "Event Ticket Offer offeredBy 'Ticketmaster'". Distinct from seller, which is a more specific term for a person or organization selling something.

candidates.label: supersededBy
candidates.comment: A deprecation relation between an older term (property, class, or enumeration) and a newer term that replaces or supersedes it. Also called "replaced by", "obsoleted by", "succeeded by", "deprecated by". Examples: "OldProperty is supersededBy NewProperty", "The deprecated class is supersededBy a modern equivalent", "This enumeration value is supersededBy a more precise one."

relations.embedding_query_text: correctedDecisionFor:

chosen_property.label: correctedDecisionFor
chosen_property.definition: Indicates the person for whom a decision was corrected by a sports referee system.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property directly indicates a SportsRefereeSystem correcting a decision for a Person.

candidates.label: correction
candidates.comment: A modification relation between a creative work and the comment, text, or document detailing a correction to it. Also called: erratum, amendment, revision, fix. Examples: "News Article" correction "Editor's Note: A previous version of this article misstated...", "Software Manual" correction "See errata sheet for updates.", "Research Paper" correction "Correction published in Vol. 15, Issue 3.".

candidates.label: isAccessoryOrSparePartFor
candidates.comment: A product compatibility relation between a product and the other products for which it serves as an accessory or spare part. Also called accessory for, spare part for, compatible with, used with. Examples: A phone case isAccessoryOrSparePartFor 'iPhone 15'. A replacement battery isAccessoryOrSparePartFor 'Laptop Model X'. A camera lens isAccessoryOrSparePartFor 'DSLR Camera Y'. Distinct from isConsumableFor, which refers to items that are used up.

candidates.label: reservationFor
candidates.comment: A reservation for relation between a reservation and the specific item or service being booked. Also called booked item, reserved item, subject of reservation. Examples: "A reservation is for 'Flight BA249'.", "A restaurant booking is for 'Dinner at The Fancy Bistro'.", "A hotel reservation is for 'Room 301'."

candidates.label: itemDefectReturnFees
candidates.comment: A return cost relation between a merchant return policy and the type of fees associated with returning defective products. Also called defect return fees, faulty item return cost, return fees for defects. Examples: A return policy has itemDefectReturnFees of 'FreeReturn'. A return policy has itemDefectReturnFees of 'RestockingFee'. A return policy has itemDefectReturnFees of 'ReturnShippingFees'. Distinct from itemDefectReturnShippingFeesAmount, which specifies the *amount* of shipping fees, not the *type* of fees.

candidates.label: dateDeleted
candidates.comment: A temporal removal relation between a data feed item and the datetime it was removed from the feed. Also called: deletion date, removal date, date of removal. Examples: "Expired Job Posting" date deleted "2023-06-30", "Outdated Product Listing" date deleted "2023-01-01T00:00:00Z".

candidates.label: supersededBy
candidates.comment: A deprecation relation between an older term (property, class, or enumeration) and a newer term that replaces or supersedes it. Also called "replaced by", "obsoleted by", "succeeded by", "deprecated by". Examples: "OldProperty is supersededBy NewProperty", "The deprecated class is supersededBy a modern equivalent", "This enumeration value is supersededBy a more precise one."

candidates.label: legislationRepeals
candidates.comment: A repeal relation between two pieces of legislation, where one cancels or abrogates the other. Also called: cancels, abrogates, revokes. Examples: "New Act legislationRepeals Old Act", "Regulation X legislationRepeals Directive Y", "Law 123 legislationRepeals Statute 456".

candidates.label: legislationAmends
candidates.comment: A legislative modification relation between a piece of legislation and another legislation that it alters or revises. Also called amends law, modifies legislation, revises act, changes statute. Examples: Legislation A legislationAmends 'Legislation B'. The new act legislationAmends 'the previous statute'. This bill legislationAmends 'the tax code'. Distinct from legislationChanges, which is a broader term for any change, whereas legislationAmends specifically introduces legal changes.

candidates.label: returnPolicySeasonalOverride
candidates.comment: A temporary modification or override of a standard merchant return policy for a specific season or period. Also called seasonal return policy change, temporary return policy, holiday return policy. Examples: `Standard Return Policy` returnPolicySeasonalOverride `Holiday Return Policy 2023`, `Summer Sale Policy` returnPolicySeasonalOverride `Extended Return Window`, `Black Friday Policy` returnPolicySeasonalOverride `Special Return Terms`.

candidates.label: dateModified
candidates.comment: A temporal revision relation between a creative work or data feed item and the date it was most recently modified. Also called: last modified date, revision date, update date. Examples: "Wikipedia Article" date modified "2023-10-26T11:45:00Z", "Software Documentation" date modified "2023-09-01", "Data Feed Entry" date modified "2023-01-05". Distinct from dateCreated, which is the initial creation date.

relations.embedding_query_text: resultedInBookingFor:

chosen_property.label: resultedInBookingFor
chosen_property.definition: Indicates the person for whom a booking (penalty) resulted from a sports referee system's action.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property directly indicates a SportsRefereeSystem resulting in a booking for a Person.

candidates.label: result
candidates.comment: The outcome or product generated by an action. Also called outcome, product, output, consequence. Examples: `WriteAction` result `Book`, `CookAction` result `Meal`, `CreateAction` result `Artwork`. Distinct from `resultComment` and `resultReview` which are specific types of results.

candidates.label: advanceBookingRequirement
candidates.comment: An advance booking requirement relation between a demand or offer and the minimum time needed between acceptance and actual usage. Also called lead time, booking lead time, reservation notice. Examples: "A flight offer's advance booking requirement is '24 hours'.", "The concert ticket demand has an advance booking requirement of '7 days'."

candidates.label: reservationFor
candidates.comment: A reservation for relation between a reservation and the specific item or service being booked. Also called booked item, reserved item, subject of reservation. Examples: "A reservation is for 'Flight BA249'.", "A restaurant booking is for 'Dinner at The Fancy Bistro'.", "A hotel reservation is for 'Room 301'."

candidates.label: resultReview
candidates.comment: The specific review created as the outcome of a review action. Also called generated review, review outcome, produced review. Examples: `ReviewAction on Product` resultReview `Customer's Product Review`, `ReviewAction on Movie` resultReview `Critic's Movie Review`, `ReviewAction on Service` resultReview `User Service Feedback`. Distinct from `result`, which is a general outcome of any action.

candidates.label: resultComment
candidates.comment: The specific comment created or sent as the outcome of a comment or reply action. Also called generated comment, comment outcome, produced comment. Examples: `CommentAction on Article` resultComment `User's Comment Text`, `ReplyAction to Forum Post` resultComment `Reply Comment`, `ReviewAction` resultComment `Reviewer's Feedback`. Distinct from `result`, which is a general outcome of any action.

candidates.label: tourBookingPage
candidates.comment: A tour booking page relation between an accommodation, apartment complex, or place and a URL providing information on how to book a tour. Also called tour reservation page, booking link for tours, tour information URL. Examples: "Hotel tourBookingPage 'https://example.com/hotel-tours'", "ApartmentComplex tourBookingPage 'https://example.com/apt-tours'", "Museum tourBookingPage 'https://example.com/museum-tours'".

candidates.label: recordedIn
candidates.comment: A recording capture relation between an event and the creative work that captured all or part of it. Also called captured by, documented in, featured in. Examples: "A concert event was recorded in 'a live album'.", "A historical event was recorded in 'a documentary film'.", "A speech event was recorded in 'a news broadcast'.". Distinct from recordedAt, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: acquiredFrom
candidates.comment: An acquired from relation between ownership information and the organization or person from whom a product was obtained. Also called purchased from, obtained from, source of acquisition. Examples: "The car's ownership info indicates it was acquired from 'Dealership X'.", "The book's ownership info shows it was acquired from 'John Doe'."

candidates.label: causeOf
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical cause and the medical entity (condition, complication, symptom) it produces. Also called "results in", "leads to", "produces". Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

candidates.label: bookEdition
candidates.comment: A textual description of the edition of a book. Also called: edition number, publication edition. Examples: "Book 'The Lord of the Rings' bookEdition 'First Edition'", "Book 'Textbook' bookEdition '2nd Edition'."

chosen_property.definition: Indicates the sports infraction for which a person was booked (received a penalty).
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property directly indicates a Person being booked for a SportsInfraction.

candidates.label: reservationFor
candidates.comment: A reservation for relation between a reservation and the specific item or service being booked. Also called booked item, reserved item, subject of reservation. Examples: "A reservation is for 'Flight BA249'.", "A restaurant booking is for 'Dinner at The Fancy Bistro'.", "A hotel reservation is for 'Room 301'."

candidates.label: bookEdition
candidates.comment: A textual description of the edition of a book. Also called: edition number, publication edition. Examples: "Book 'The Lord of the Rings' bookEdition 'First Edition'", "Book 'Textbook' bookEdition '2nd Edition'."

candidates.label: bookingAgent
candidates.comment: An organization or person acting as a broker or booking agent for a reservation. Also called: reservation agent, travel agent, broker. Examples: "Reservation 'Hotel Stay' bookingAgent 'Booking.com'", "Reservation 'Flight' bookingAgent 'Travel Agency X'."

candidates.label: bookingTime
candidates.comment: A date and time when a reservation was booked. Also called: reservation time, booking date. Examples: "Reservation 'Restaurant' bookingTime '2023-10-26T19:00:00'", "Reservation 'Car Rental' bookingTime '2023-10-25'."

candidates.label: underName
candidates.comment: An under name relation between a reservation or ticket and the organization or person for whom it is made. Also called booked for, reserved for, ticket holder. Examples: "Reservation underName 'John Doe'", "Ticket underName 'Acme Corp'", "Flight reservation underName 'Jane Smith'".

candidates.label: validFor
candidates.comment: A valid for relation between a credential or permit and the duration of its validity. Also called duration of validity, valid period, effective duration. Examples: "Permit validFor 'P1Y'", "Credential validFor 'P5Y'", "License validFor 'P6M'".

candidates.label: reservationStatus
candidates.comment: A reservation status relation between a reservation and its current state, such as confirmed or cancelled. Also called booking status, status of reservation. Examples: "A flight reservation has a reservation status 'Confirmed'.", "A hotel booking has a reservation status 'Pending'.", "A restaurant reservation has a reservation status 'Cancelled'."

candidates.label: tourBookingPage
candidates.comment: A tour booking page relation between an accommodation, apartment complex, or place and a URL providing information on how to book a tour. Also called tour reservation page, booking link for tours, tour information URL. Examples: "Hotel tourBookingPage 'https://example.com/hotel-tours'", "ApartmentComplex tourBookingPage 'https://example.com/apt-tours'", "Museum tourBookingPage 'https://example.com/museum-tours'".

candidates.label: reservationId
candidates.comment: A reservation ID relation between a reservation and its unique alphanumeric identifier. Also called booking ID, confirmation number. Examples: "A flight reservation has a reservation ID 'ABCDEF'.", "A hotel booking has a reservation ID 'H123456'.", "A car rental reservation has a reservation ID 'CR7890'."

candidates.label: ticketNumber
candidates.comment: A unique textual identifier for a ticket. Also called "ticket ID", "booking number", "reference number", "ticket code". Examples: "The concert ticket has ticketNumber 'ABC123XYZ'", "The flight ticket's ticketNumber is a unique alphanumeric code", "This ticket is identified by its ticketNumber."

chosen_property.label: isDescribedAs
chosen_property.definition: Indicates that a sports event is described as a particular observation.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property directly indicates a SportsEvent being described as an Observation.

candidates.label: isRelatedTo
candidates.comment: A general association relation between two products or services that have some unspecified connection. Also called associated with, connected to, linked to, relevant to. Examples: A smartphone isRelatedTo 'a smart watch'. A car service isRelatedTo 'car insurance'. A book isRelatedTo 'a movie adaptation'. Distinct from isSimilarTo, which implies functional similarity, and isAccessoryOrSparePartFor or isConsumableFor, which imply specific functional dependencies. This is a very general relation.

candidates.label: isrcCode
candidates.comment: A music recording identification relation between a music recording and its International Standard Recording Code. Also called ISRC identifier, recording code, music track ID. Examples: A music recording has an isrcCode of 'US-S1Z-99-00001'. A song has an isrcCode of 'GB-LFB-04-00001'. An album track has an isrcCode of 'QZ-F89-12-00001'. Distinct from iswcCode, which is for musical compositions, not recordings.

candidates.label: isicV4
candidates.comment: An industry classification relation between an organization, person, or place and its International Standard Industrial Classification of All Economic Activities (ISIC) Revision 4 code. Also called ISIC code, industry classification code, economic activity code. Examples: An organization has an isicV4 of '6201' (Computer programming activities). A person has an isicV4 of '8620' (Medical and dental practice activities). A place has an isicV4 of '5510' (Hotels and similar accommodation).

candidates.label: isResizable
candidates.comment: A model property relation indicating whether a 3D model can be scaled or resized. Also called resizable, scalable, adjustable size. Examples: A 3D model of a chair has isResizable set to 'true'. A 3D model of a building has isResizable set to 'false'. A 3D model of a character has isResizable set to 'true'.

candidates.label: isPartOf
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation indicating that an item or creative work is a component of a larger creative work or resource. Also called component of, member of, contained in, element of. Examples: A chapter isPartOf 'a book'. An episode isPartOf 'a TV series'. A web page isPartOf 'a website'. Distinct from hasPart, which expresses the inverse relationship (the whole *has* a part).

candidates.label: member
candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: belongs to, is a part of, participant in. Examples: "Club Organization member John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership member Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization member Partner Company". Distinct from memberOf, which expresses the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: iswcCode
candidates.comment: A music composition identification relation between a music composition and its International Standard Musical Work Code. Also called ISWC identifier, composition code, musical work ID. Examples: A music composition has an iswcCode of 'T-034.045.001-6'. A song has an iswcCode of 'T-901.234.567-8'. A classical piece has an iswcCode of 'T-123.456.789-0'. Distinct from isrcCode, which is for music recordings, not compositions.

candidates.label: isVariantOf
candidates.comment: A product variation relation between a product or product model and the base product or product group from which it is a specific variant. Also called variant of, version of, derived from product, specific model of. Examples: A 'red iPhone 15' isVariantOf 'iPhone 15 Pro'. A 'size L t-shirt' isVariantOf 'Basic T-Shirt ProductGroup'. A 'diesel car model' isVariantOf 'Car Model X'. Distinct from isRelatedTo or isSimilarTo, as it implies a direct hierarchical relationship of variation from a base product or group.

candidates.label: memberOf
candidates.comment: A membership relation between an organization or person and the organization or program membership they belong to. Also called: belongs to, is a member of, affiliated with. Examples: "John Doe memberOf 'Local Sports Club'", "Acme Corp memberOf 'Industry Association'", "Jane Smith memberOf 'Premium Membership Tier'". Distinct from member, which expresses the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: isGift
candidates.comment: A transaction intent relation indicating whether an order was placed as a gift for a recipient other than the buyer. Also called gift purchase, purchased as gift, gift order. Examples: An order has isGift set to 'true'. A purchase has isGift set to 'false'. A book order has isGift set to 'true' with gift wrapping.

chosen_property.label: broadcastsEvent

candidates.label: broadcastSubChannel
candidates.comment: A subchannel identification for a broadcast frequency specification. Also called "subchannel of broadcast", "broadcast channel identifier". Examples: "FM 98.1 specification broadcastSubChannel 'HD2'", "Digital TV channel 5 specification broadcastSubChannel '5.3'".

candidates.label: broadcaster
candidates.comment: An ownership or operational relation between a broadcast service and the organization responsible for it. Also called "service provider", "operated by", "owned by", "broadcast by". Examples: "BBC Radio 4 broadcaster BBC", "CNN broadcast service broadcaster Warner Bros. Discovery".

candidates.label: broadcastOfEvent
candidates.comment: An event that is being broadcast by a broadcast event. Also called: televised event, event broadcast. Examples: "BroadcastEvent 'Super Bowl Live' broadcastOfEvent 'Super Bowl LVIII'", "BroadcastEvent 'Concert Stream' broadcastOfEvent 'Live Music Concert'."

candidates.label: broadcastAffiliateOf
candidates.comment: An organization representing the media network(s) whose content is broadcast on a broadcast service. Also called: network affiliation, broadcast network. Examples: "BroadcastService 'Local TV Station' broadcastAffiliateOf 'NBC'", "BroadcastService 'Radio Station' broadcastAffiliateOf 'NPR'."

candidates.label: broadcastServiceTier
candidates.comment: A textual description of the type of service required to access a broadcast channel. Also called: channel tier, service level, subscription tier. Examples: "BroadcastChannel 'Premium Movies' broadcastServiceTier 'Premium'", "BroadcastChannel 'Basic News' broadcastServiceTier 'Standard'."

candidates.label: isLiveBroadcast
candidates.comment: A broadcast status relation indicating whether a broadcast event is being transmitted in real-time. Also called live stream, real-time broadcast, live transmission. Examples: A sports game broadcast has isLiveBroadcast set to 'true'. A news report broadcast has isLiveBroadcast set to 'true'. A recorded TV show broadcast has isLiveBroadcast set to 'false'.

candidates.label: broadcastSignalModulation
candidates.comment: A qualitative value or text describing the modulation (e.g., FM, AM) used by a particular broadcast service. Also called: signal modulation, broadcast modulation type. Examples: "BroadcastFrequencySpecification 'Radio Station' broadcastSignalModulation 'FM'", "BroadcastFrequencySpecification 'AM Station' broadcastSignalModulation 'AM'."

candidates.label: broadcastFrequency
candidates.comment: A frequency used for over-the-air broadcasts for a broadcast channel or service. Also called: broadcast frequency, radio frequency, channel frequency. Examples: "BroadcastChannel 'FM Station' broadcastFrequency '87.9 FM'", "BroadcastService 'TV Channel' broadcastFrequency 'BroadcastFrequencySpecification 500 MHz'."

candidates.label: broadcastDisplayName
candidates.comment: A name displayed in the channel guide for a broadcast service. Also called: channel name, station display name. Examples: "BroadcastService 'Local News' broadcastDisplayName 'WXYZ-TV'", "BroadcastService 'Music Radio' broadcastDisplayName 'KEXP 90.3 FM'."

candidates.label: hasBroadcastChannel
candidates.comment: A channel association relation between a broadcast service and one of its broadcast channels. Also called includes channel, offers channel, channel of. Examples: "A TV service has a broadcast channel for news.", "A radio service has a broadcast channel for music.", "The streaming service has a broadcast channel for sports."
